transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood); Maya Patel, Jon Rivera, Sara Li (VeraHealth)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Maya Patel: yep, loud and clear.
[00:10] Alex Chen: quick agenda - go through last week's benchmark numbers vs your baseline provider, call out where we saw wins and regressions, talk tuning knobs (batching, kv cache, quant, seq len), then next steps. sound good?
[00:20] Jon Rivera: yep that's fine. we've got the infra folks on the line to ask about network stuff.

Summary / quick results
[02:00] Priya Nair: ok so in the test we've been running, p50 latency for your live traffic profile: baseline provider was about 120ms, Redwood hosted at default config hit ~85ms, and Redwood with kv prewarm + batching got down to ~60ms p50. p95 numbers: baseline ~420ms, Redwood default ~230ms, tuned ~190-210ms. throughput: baseline peak 180 reqs/sec, Redwood tuned sustained 320 reqs/sec for same model and sequence length.
[02:45] Maya Patel: those numbers look promising, the p95 drop is most interesting for our user-facing flows. i guess question is are these apples to apples?
[03:10] Priya Nair: good point - we tried to match sequence length distribution and request size, we pushed same prompt sets. there are small diffs: baseline was on v2 model variant with 16-bit floats, we ran the open model with 8-bit quant on Redwood for the tuned runs which helped throughput. there might be slight quality delta on some prompts but we ran a quick eval set and didn't see major regressions.
[03:45] Sara Li: small clarifying q - when you say tuning, you meant quantization + kv cache + batching right?
[03:50] Priya Nair: yep, exactly. kv cache (we sometimes see it transcribed as K-V cash in notes, haha) for repeated prefix reuse, dynamic batching up to 32, and 8-bit quant to improve memory bandwidth.

Latency deep dive
[08:00] Alex Chen: walking through the p95 reduction: biggest gains came from two places - the kv cache (prefix reuse) cut the token generation time on repeat contexts by ~25%, and batching improved amortized kernel launch overhead. on our infra we also have improved kernel selection for the attention op which helps long seqs.
[09:00] Jon Rivera: curious about network hops - our baseline tests were run in us-east-1 also, but they had different peering. did you do anything special with TCP or keepalives?
[09:20] Priya Nair: we kept the same az, but we turned on connection pooling and re-used sessions aggressively; that plus tail latency mitigation policies in Redwood's serving runtime reduces p95 noise. also if you go Dedicated, you get less noisy neighbors which can tighten p95.
[10:05] Maya Patel: any regressions to flag?
[10:10] Priya Nair: minimal - a few prompts on the eval set showed slightly different tokens when using 8-bit quant, mostly punctuation and formatting, no critical semantic drift. we flagged those in the eval sheet.

Throughput / cost tradeoffs
[13:30] Alex Chen: for throughput the baseline was CPU constrained on their config; with GPU and batching we hit the 320 req/s number while keeping cost per token lower. important tradeoff - larger batch sizes improve throughput but raise p50 for single interactive calls. we recommended dynamic batching thresholds to keep tail latency within your SLOs.
[14:20] Sara Li: can you give a rough cost delta?
[14:30] Priya Nair: high level - on the test footprint we estimate 15-25% lower per-token cost when using Redwood hosted tuned config vs baseline provider; Dedicated pricing will change the math - we'll send a detailed cost sheet.

Quality / evaluation notes
[18:00] Priya Nair: quality eval: we ran 1k prompt comparisons, about 94% exact intent parity, 6% minor format/phrase diffs. we included the eval csv in the shared drive link.
[18:30] Maya Patel: can you share that link again?
[18:40] Alex Chen: yes, i'll drop it in the followup. link: <redwood-shared/verahealth/poc/benchmarks.csv> (placeholder)

Security / deployment constraints
[21:00] Jon Rivera: we need VPC peering and our security team wants KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. baseline provider had centralized key management. what does Redwood's private option give us?
[21:30] Priya Nair: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM in the private control plane, audit logging, and VPC peering. for on-prem we can do an appliance but that takes longer. we'll share SOC2/ISO docs; a note in the security doc said SAML SSO + RBAC are supported.
[22:10] Jon Rivera: good, for perf we might need to run an on-prem spike to see actual rack-level hops.
[22:20] Alex Chen: we can do that as an optional run.

Tuning knobs discussed
[25:00] Priya Nair: knobs recap: 1) Batch size (dynamic) 2) KV cache TTL / prewarm strategy 3) Quant levels (8-bit, 4-bit for more gain but more quality risk) 4) Model sharding and kernel selection for long seqs.
[26:10] Maya Patel: what's your recommendation for us initially?
[26:15] Priya Nair: start with 8-bit quant + kv prewarm + conservative batching (max 16) to preserve p50, run a week of traffic with monitoring; then iterate to increase batch ceiling if p95 tolerances hold.

Objections and constraints
[30:00] Sara Li: product is worried about tiny semantic diffs from quant. our user-study is sensitive to wording.
[30:15] Priya Nair: understood - we can run A/B test with 10% traffic to quant branch and monitor key metrics (NPS-ish, error rates). also we can do fallback to full-precision under specific routes.

Recap and explicit next steps
[36:00] Alex Chen: recap - we'll share raw CSV, evaluation sheets, and a tuned config recommendation. customer will confirm test dataset/traffic; we'll run an on-prem spike if you want. next call proposed same time next week to review updated numbers.
[36:30] Maya Patel: agreed.
[36:40] Jon Rivera: i'll open a ticket with our networking team and share contact.
[37:00] Sara Li: i'll pull product stakeholders into the next sync.

Closing micro-notes (transcription imperfections)
[40:00] Speaker 1: um yeah, so the ESL-A doc, ESL-A, I mean SLA, was mentioned a few times - transcription sometimes swaps acronyms.
[40:20] Priya Nair: noted, we'll include a clean pdf of the security pack in the followup.

End of transcript.

References and shared artifacts: bench CSV link (shared), evaluation CSV, security pack (SOC2/ISO/SSO), Dedicated pricing sheet (will be sent).
